title: Role of Gd 5d-Au 5d hybridization for the magnetic properties of Au-Al-Gd quasicrystal approximants
authors: Goro Nozue, Hidenori Fujiwara, Satoru Hamamoto, Yuto Torii, Mai Sakaguchi, Sho Nakajima, Takuya D. Nakamura, Nonoka U. Sakamoto, Takayuki Kiss, Masaki Oura, Akira Yasui, Kotaro Higashi, Naomi Kawamura, Kojiro Mimura, Arata Tanaka, Asuka Ishikawa, Farid Labib, Shintaro Suzuki, Takafumi D. Yamamoto, Ryuji Tamura, Akira Sekiyama
abstract: We have studied the electronic states of magnetic Au-Al-Gd quasicrystal approximants, which exhibit different magnetic ground states at low temperatures, by orbital-selective soft and hard x-ray electron spectroscopies in the paramagnetic phase. Our results reveal that the valence electronic states vary among the Au-Al-Gd approximants with different magnetic ground states, whereas the Gd 4f electrons are localized in all of them. In particular, we find that the Gd 5d states are hybridized with the Au 5d states around the Fermi level, providing information about a local pathway for the intersite exchange interaction between the localized Gd 4f electrons. This hybridization strength varies among these samples. Our findings bring an orbital-resolved microscopic picture to the magnetism of rare-earth-based quasicrystals and approximants.
summary: This work uses advanced x-ray spectroscopy to investigate the electronic structure of Au-Al-Gd quasicrystal approximants exhibiting different magnetic states. The key finding is that the magnetic behavior is dictated by the hybridization between Gd 5d and Au 5d orbitals near the Fermi level. This provides a detailed, orbital-resolved picture of the magnetic exchange interaction in these rare-earth-based quasicrystals.
main_problem: To understand the relationship between the valence electronic states and the magnetic properties of Au-Al-Gd quasicrystal approximants, specifically elucidating the mechanism of intersite exchange interaction between localized Gd 4f electrons.
main_result: The magnetic properties are governed by hybridization between the Gd 5d and Au 5d states near the Fermi level, and the strength of this hybridization varies significantly depending on the magnetic ground state (AFM, FM, or SG).
method: The study employed orbital-selective soft and hard x-ray electron spectroscopies (HAXPES, XAS, RPES) performed in the paramagnetic phase to probe the electronic structure.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Au-Al-Gd quasicrystal approximants (ACs), which exhibit distinct magnetic ground states (AFM, FM, SG) correlated with the electron-per-atom ratio.
key_observables: Valence electronic states, hybridization strength between Gd 5d and Au 5d states, and the magnetic ground state (AFM, FM, SG).
important_parameters: The electron-per-atom ratio (e/a) and the specific chemical composition of the approximants.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed hybridization provides a microscopic pathway for the intersite exchange interaction, moving beyond models relying solely on the Fermi wavenumber.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of magnetic properties on the e/a ratio, and show core-level XAS and photoemission spectra for the three magnetic phases, confirming localized Gd 4f states.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the electronic structure using multiple spectroscopic techniques to correlate the observed valence state variations (especially Gd 5d-Au 5d hybridization) with the established magnetic ground states across different compositions.
why_interesting: The detailed orbital-resolved spectroscopy provides a direct, microscopic link between hybridization mechanisms (Gd 5d-Au 5d) and macroscopic magnetic ordering in complex, quasiperiodic materials.
